name: AZ-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Stanton's roughly four-to-one fundraising and cash advantage with no outside spending against him
Incumbency in a D+4 district with a favorable Democratic environment
Prediction markets price Stanton's reelection near 96 percent
No public general-election polling, keeping the margin estimate broad
model.rationale: Stanton holds a dominant financial position, faces a little-funded challenger with no outside opposition, and markets price his reelection around 96 percent; district fundamentals and the incumbent edge point to a comfortable double-digit Democratic margin despite the absence of polling.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Stanton or the first public polls showing a single-digit race would be the clearest signal to move this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Greg Stanton, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in this Phoenix-area district that leans Democratic by about four points. He has raised roughly $2.1 million and holds about $2.0 million on hand, while Republican challenger Zuhdi Jasser has raised about $565,000. No outside groups are spending against Stanton, and a Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot. Prediction markets give Stanton roughly a 96 percent chance of winning.

No public general-election polls are available for this race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial advantage, and market pricing. Those indicators point to a comfortable Stanton win, with the national environment adding to the Democratic edge. The main uncertainty is the lack of polling, which keeps the margin estimate wide; late opposition spending or unexpected survey data would be the most likely sources of change.
